Definition: from G2095 and the same as G4332; sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service):--X attend upon.
BiblicalUsage: Euprosedros means to attend without distraction, and it stands in 1 Corinthians 7:35, where Paul says he writes so that the unmarried may attend upon the Lord without distraction. The verse is a Textus Receptus reading: the SBL text at 1 Corinthians 7:35 reads euparedron instead, the same sense in a different word.
TheologicalSignificance: I take euprosedros as it stands: to attend without distraction.
